title: Web Workers overview and limits
learningObjectives: Explain web workers overview and limits and use the browser API with appropriate lifecycle and privacy safeguards.

understand.concept: Web Workers run JavaScript in a separate worker context, allowing CPU-heavy work to run away from the main UI thread. They communicate through message passing and structured cloning or transferable objects. Workers do not have direct access to the DOM or window.
understand.whyItMatters: Workers can keep the interface responsive during expensive computation. They add messaging and lifecycle complexity and cannot replace main-thread DOM work.
understand.analogy: A worker is a helper in another room: it can process data and send results, but it cannot directly rearrange the main room's DOM.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; browser API support, permission, lifecycle, and security rules vary by platform.

explain.narrative: The main thread sends data and receives a message. worker.js must listen for message and post a result.

examples.explanation: The main thread sends data and receives a message. worker.js must listen for message and post a result.
examples.expectedOutput: Browser console or UI output demonstrates the API; permission and secure-context features require a supported environment.

practise.guidedTask: Move a CPU-heavy calculation into a worker. Measure UI responsiveness and terminate the worker when no longer needed.
practise.independentTask: Build a small feature using the API. Include feature detection, permission or failure handling, cleanup, and an accessible alternative where relevant.
hints: Do not assume the API is available in every browser.
Request sensitive permissions only after explaining why.
Clean up observers, workers, and listeners when no longer needed.

questions.prompt: Can a Web Worker directly manipulate the page DOM?
questions.explanation: Workers do not have direct access to the document DOM.

questions.prompt: What is a reliable approach when using browser APIs?
options: Feature-detect, handle denial or failure, and clean up resources
questions.answer: Feature-detect, handle denial or failure, and clean up resources
questions.explanation: Browser features need graceful fallback, privacy-aware permission, and lifecycle management.
